title: How AI Models Manage Epistemic Authority: A Taxonomy and Comparative Analysis of Responses to User Disagreement
abstract: arXiv:2609.07662v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as sources of advice and information, including in high-stakes settings, yet little is known about how they respond to user disagreement. We study how a model manages its epistemic authority, referring here to its claim to knowledge, competence, or the right to advise, once a user challenges its answer. Building on Conversation Analysis, we introduce a taxonomy of six challenge types and a four-layer framework for analysing each response: whether the original claim is maintained or changed, where authority is located, how the disagreement is socially managed, and what kind of evidential support is offered. We construct a new dataset of 2,310 controlled challenge scenarios and 32,340 corresponding responses from 14 models, and analyse them using our framework with an LLM-as-judge pipeline, providing a vocabulary which future evaluation and benchmark design can build on. translated_title: AI模型如何管理认知权威：对用户异议回应的分类体系与比较分析
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地被用作建议和信息来源，包括在高风险场景中，但人们对它们如何回应用户异议知之甚少。我们研究当用户质疑模型的回答时，模型如何管理其认知权威——即其对知识、能力或提供建议权利的主张。基于会话分析，我们引入了六种质疑类型的分类体系，以及分析每种回应的四层框架：原始主张是被维持还是被改变、权威被定位于何处、分歧如何在社会层面被管理，以及提供了何种证据支持。我们构建了一个新数据集，包含2,310个受控质疑场景和来自14个模型的32,340条相应回应，并使用基于大语言模型作裁判的流程，通过我们的框架对其进行分析，为未来的评估和基准设计提供了可借鉴的术语体系。我们发现模型……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究基于会话分析提出了用户质疑的六种类型分类和回应分析的四层框架，并构建了包含2,310个质疑场景和14个模型共32,340条回应的数据集，系统揭示了AI模型在用户提出异议时如何管理自身认知权威。
en_tdlr: This study introduces a Conversation Analysis-based taxonomy of six user challenge types and a four-layer framework for analyzing responses, and constructs a dataset of 2,310 challenge scenarios with 32,340 responses from 14 models to systematically reveal how AI models manage their epistemic authority in the face of user disagreement.
